subject: chemical
audience: FE Chemical candidates and chemical engineering students
title: The Batch Reactor That Reached 63%, Not 100%
featured_title: THE BATCH REACTOR THAT REACHED 63 PERCENT, NOT 100

presentation.challenge: The shortcut kt=1 suggested 100% conversion after 5 minutes. The first-order batch model gave only 63.2%.

practice.primary_question: How is conversion calculated for an irreversible first-order reaction in a constant-volume batch reactor?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using the linear approximation X=kt at moderate or large kt instead of the exponential first-order batch relation.

case_dna.target_misconception: For a first-order batch reaction, conversion after time t is X=kt for all values of kt.
case_dna.why_plausible: At very small kt, 1-exp(-kt) is approximately kt, so the shortcut can look valid in early-time calculations.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For k=0.20 min^-1 and t=5.0 min, kt=1.0 but X=1-exp(-1)=0.6321, not 1.000.
case_dna.corrected_model: For an irreversible first-order reaction in a constant-volume batch reactor, CA=CA0 exp(-kt) and X=1-exp(-kt).

problem_statement: A constant-volume batch reactor carries out an irreversible first-order reaction A→products with k=0.20 min^-1. A note uses X=kt and predicts complete conversion after 5.0 min. Determine the correct conversion. Then determine the time required for 90% conversion at the same rate constant.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The linear shortcut predicted complete conversion too early.
gates.prompt: Which integrated rate law should govern the remaining concentration?

options.label: Use CA/CA0=exp(-kt), so X=1-exp(-kt)
options.reason: This is the integrated first-order rate law for the stated constant-volume batch reactor.

options.label: Use X=kt for all times
options.reason: That is only a small-kt approximation and can exceed the physical limit X=1.

options.label: Use X=kt/(1+kt)
options.reason: That form is not the integrated first-order batch relation.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Run the batch for 5 minutes
gates.result: The batch reaches about 63.2% conversion after 5.0 min.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the batch conversion
gates.hint: Use the exponential integrated rate law, not X=kt.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The remaining reactant follows exponential decay

cards.text: The linear result X=1.0 overpredicts conversion by 36.8 percentage points.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the batch calculation note
report: C1. The reaction is first order with k=0.20 min^-1.
C2. The batch runs for 5.0 min.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is a stated kinetic parameter.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated reaction time.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It replaces the integrated first-order relation with an invalid linear shortcut.

evidence_choices.label: X=1-exp(-1)=0.6321
evidence_choices.reason: This follows directly from the integrated first-order batch equation.

correction.template: The batch conversion after 5.0 min is about {conversion}%.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reach 90% conversion with the same kinetics
gates.constraint: Keep k=0.20 min^-1 and the same first-order batch model.

options.label: Run for 4.50 min
options.reason: This comes from the invalid linear relation X=kt.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same kinetics at a lower rate constant
gates.prompt: If k=0.10 min^-1 and t=5.0 min, what conversion is obtained?

options.reason: That again uses X=kt as an exact equation.

options.label: About 60.65%
options.reason: That is the fraction of A remaining, exp(-0.5).

gates.explanation: The first-order batch conversion is X=1-exp(-kt).

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the batch-reactor calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that first-order batch conversion follows the integrated exponential rate law, not the linear approximation at arbitrary time.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A small-time approximation was treated as an exact conversion equation.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use X=1-exp(-kt) for the stated constant-volume first-order batch reactor.

seo.seo_title: First-Order Batch Reactor Conversion: 63.2% at kt=1 | FE E-067
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Chemical Case E-067: a first-order batch reactor with k=0.20 min^-1 reaches 63.2% conversion after 5 minutes, not 100%.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Chemical first order batch reactor conversion
seo.excerpt: A first-order batch reactor does not follow X=kt except as a small-time approximation. The exact conversion is exponential.
seo.direct_answer: For a constant-volume first-order batch reactor, X=1-exp(-kt). With k=0.20 min^-1 and t=5.0 min, X=1-exp(-1)=0.6321, or 63.2%. Reaching 90% conversion requires t=-ln(0.10)/0.20=11.51 min.

faqs.q: What is the first-order batch-reactor conversion equation?
faqs.a: For the stated constant-volume irreversible reaction, X=1-exp(-kt).

faqs.q: How long does 90% conversion take when k=0.20 min^-1?
